name: BYTEDANCE + DEERFLOW
text: The TikTok parent open-sourced DeerFlow (Deep Exploration and Efficient Research Flow), a "SuperAgent harness" designed for deep research automation. Think of it as a unified controller for complex AI agent workflows.

name: ALIBABA QWEN
text: Junyang Lin, lead architect of the Qwen model series, has departed following a major infrastructure push. The move raises questions about continuity at one of China's most aggressive open-source AI labs.

name: NVIDIA
text: Entering the open-source agent wars: NemoClaw is the chip giant’s upcoming platform for building autonomous AI agents, signaling a strategic pivot toward infrastructure software.

name: META + MOLTBOOK
text: Moltbook, the viral "social network where AI agents talk to each other." The deal suggests Meta sees agent-to-agent interaction as the next social graph frontier.

name: CHINA
text: China’s embrace of OpenClaw is igniting a rally in domestic AI stocks. Zhipu, Tencent, and MiniMax are racing to integrate the open-source framework, while government agencies move to deploy it across state and enterprise systems: balancing rapid AI turnaround with tightened security access protocols.

name: ANDREJ KARPATHY
text: Released an Auto Research Agent framework designed for distributed ML collaboration. Agents can share experiment results in real-time, creating a collective learning network for open research.

name: NOUS RESEARCH
text: Dropped Hermes Agent v0.2.0 one month post-launch: 216 PRs merged, 63 contributors, 119 issues resolved. It's a persistent server-side AI that learns over runtime. Plus they threw a hackathon with wild consumer builds: a Signal bot and a self-playing Pokémon agent.

name: OPENFANG
text: OpenFang is an open-source Agent OS written entirely in Rust - 137K lines of code that compiles down to a single 32MB binary.

name: EVOSKILL
text: Sentient AI Researcher Salah Alzu'bi published a framework for self-evolving agents that learn by failing. EvoSkill automatically discovers and refines skills through iterative failure analysis, removing the need for manual capability programming.

name: ARENA UNDERWAY
text: 500+ applications. The first cohort is in. Starting March 14, they’ll spend three weeks (through April 5) tackling the real challenge in enterprise AI: reasoning accurately across massive datasets. If you're in San Francisco, come through to our events and co work with us. Ice cream on us.

name: MISTRAL + NVIDIA
text: Mistral AI partners with NVIDIA to co-develop cutting-edge open-source AI models as a founding member of the Nemotron Coalition. The initiative unites AI labs across the globe to build the best models using shared expertise and compute.

name: LINUX
text: The Linux Foundation announces $12.5M in grant funding from leading tech and AI companies which include Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, in order to advance open source security.

name: ALIBABA
text: Alibaba Cloud releases a deployment guide for CoPaw, an open-source personal AI assistant similar to OpenClaw that can be deployed on your own hardware or on the cloud. The project integrates natively with messaging platforms such as Discord and iMessage.

name: AI2
text: Non-profit AI research institute Ai2 releases MolmoWeb, an open-source visual web agent that completes tasks directly in your browser by interpreting screenshots. It’s designed to be run locally or via cloud services.

name: SORA + CLEM DELANGUE
text: OpenAI is shutting down its video generation app with exact timelines and details on preserving user work to follow. Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue suggests that OpenAI should open-source Sora as it would be “an amazing contribution to the field” and honor the efforts of the teams involved.

name: COHERE
text: Cohere Transcribe is an open-source speech-to-text model that turns minutes of audio into transcripts in seconds. At launch, it took the top spot for English language accuracy on HuggingFace’s Open ASR model leaderboard.

name: AI RESEARCH AGENTS
text: Singularity Speedrun ahead? A Tokyo-based AI lab, Sakana AI dropped The AI Scientist, a fully automated research system, and its github exploded: 12K stars and 1.8K forks in 24 hours. The premise: an AI that can ideate, code, run experiments, and write papers start-to-finish. Running parallel, Physical Superintelligence PBC open-sourced GPD (Get Physics Done)—a specialized agentic physicist that scopes problems, executes derivations, runs numerical verification, and sanity-checks its results against actual physical constraints. One system generates knowledge; the other respects the laws of nature while doing it. [ai scientist github] [get-physics-done github]

name: CRYPTOANALYSTBENCH PAPER
text: Sentient researchers release a new paper on why multi-tool, long-form reasoning agents can look fluent and still break real workflows. Their work studies the errors that emerge when agents answer open-ended questions with no clear answer.

name: THE ARENA MURDERS
text: Join us for an immersive murder mystery where the top AI builders won't be training models, they'll be solving crimes.

name: ARENA JEOPARDY
text: AI developers and founders go head to head in a trivia showdown spanning machine learning, crypto, pop culture, and more.

name: ARENA DEMO DAY
text: Cohort 0 takes the stage to demo their AI projects and mark the close of Sentient Arena’s inaugural hackathon residency.

name: SENTIENT SALON KOREA
text: Our flagship Sentient Salon series is back in Seoul, Korea. Builders, researchers, and VCs are invited for panel discussions tackling real problems and a happy hour where collaborations form. Apply early to secure your spot.

name: ANTHROPIC
text: A software engineer discovered a version of Claude Code that shipped with a source map file including a fully readable version of its source code. Within a day it was cloned and spawned multiple open-source projects such as claw-code, a rewrite that is now the fastest-growing Github repo in history at 178K stars, overtaking Anthropic’s own Claude Code repository.

name: NETFLIX
text: Netflix drops its first ever open-source AI model on HuggingFace called VOID (Video Object and Interaction Deletion). This tool not only allows objects to be deleted from a scene, it also simulates how the physics around the scene should behave once that object is gone.

name: ALIBABA QWEN
text: Alibaba Qwen drops Qwen3.6-Plus promising increased multimodal reasoning, a 1M context window, and a significant leap in its agentic coding capabilities. While the model is currently closed and only available through their official API, Alibaba plans to release smaller open-source variants of this model in the future.

name: AUTOAGENT
text: AutoAgent is an open-source library for self-improving agents that outperform human-tuned systems with no constant prompting required. The team credits this success to “model empathy,” the idea that agents improve themselves better than humans who project their instincts onto systems that think differently. Along these veins, Sentient Labs released its autoresearch toolkit for agent skills called EvoSkill, which is available for pre-release testing for all Arena participants. [JOIN ARENA DISCORD]

name: GOOGLE
text: Google has released Gemma 4, a family of open-weight models under the Apache 2.0 license that allows users to distribute, modify, and even sell the software without royalties. It comes in four sizes, with the E2B/E4B variants designed to run on mobile devices offline, by prioritizing efficiency to minimize RAM and battery usage.

name: MILLA JOVOVICH
text: Resident Evil actress Milla Jovovich creates an open-source AI memory system for Claude called MemPalace. Rather than sending your data to the cloud, it claims to mine and organize your conversations locally in a way that mirrors human memory.

name: Z.AI
text: Beijing-based AI company Z.ai has released its latest flagship model GLM 5.1, which it describes as “the next level of open source.” Built specifically for agentic engineering, the model also features improved coding capabilities and enhanced performance on long-horizon tasks, with the ability to run autonomously for up to 8 hours. [ref ]

name: SENTIENT SPARKS
text: Meet the new members joining the second batch of Sentient Sparks, our contributor program for community leaders, builders, and creators supporting Sentient’s mission to advance open-source AI.

name: SENTIENT SALON AT SEOUL
text: Sentient is heading to Seoul for a series of events bringing together builders, founders, and developers to discuss open-source AI and finance.

name: KRONOS
text: Researchers at Tsinghua University have released Kronos, the first open-source foundation model purpose-built for financial candlestick data. Pre-trained on over 12 billion records from 45 global exchanges, Kronos tokenizes market data and predicts future sequences autoregressively, which is the same paradigm LLMs use for text.

name: KIMI K2.6
text: Moonshot AI has released Kimi K2.6, a 1T-parameter open-weight MoE with 32B active per token and a 256K context window. Another strong entrant from the Chinese open-source wave, this latest model offers support for motion rich frontends, long-horizon coding, and 24/7 autonomous agents.

name: DEEPSEEK V4
text: DeepSeek has open-sourced V4, its most significant release since R1. Two variants launched: V4-Pro and V4-Flash, both supporting a 1M token context window. Released under MIT license with weights on Hugging Face, V4-Pro’s API pricing comes in at roughly 1/20th the cost of Claude Opus 4.7. The model is also the first Chinese frontier model natively optimized for Huawei Ascend chips, a milestone for non-Nvidia AI infrastructure.

name: MISTRAL MEDIUM 3.5
text: Mistral consolidates three models into one dense 128B release (77.6% SWE-Bench Verified) and ships with Vibe remote coding agents. The only EU-headquartered lab still competing at the open-source frontier.

name: NVIDIA’S ISING
text: NVIDIA has released NVIDIA Ising, the world's first family of open-source quantum AI models. Two models launched: Ising Calibration, a vision-language model that powers AI agents, and Ising Decoding, a 3D neural network for real-time quantum error correction. NVIDIA is also shipping quantum workflows and training data so builders can fine-tune on their own hardware.

name: OLLAMA + GITHUB COPILOT CLI
text: Local model runtime Ollama has added GitHub Copilot CLI to its ollama launch integrations, letting developers run GitHub's terminal coding agent against open-weight models like qwen3.5, kimi-k2.5:cloud, and glm-5.1:cloud instead of GitHub-hosted ones.

name: OPENAI’S SYMPHONY
text: OpenAI has open-sourced Symphony, a spec enabling Codex agents to read tickets from a project board, spawn a dedicated agent workspace per issue, and work autonomously until the task is ready for handoff. This has resulted in a 500% increase in landed PRs in some internal teams.

name: SENTIENT’S EVOSKILL
text: Sentient Labs released v1.1.0 of EvoSkill - an automated skill discovery tool for agents. AI engineers and researchers can enjoy added support for running the EvoSkill loop on remote environments using Docker and Daytona, as well as an OfficeQA demo.

name: PENTAGON
text: The U.S. Department of War has signed agreements with eight frontier AI companies to deploy their models on classified networks. The Pentagon will be partnering with Nvidia and Reflection to expand to open-source model providers, while the remaining six will be split between closed-models (OpenAI, Google) and infrastructure/cloud providers (Microsoft, AWS, Oracle, SpaceX).

name: MEET OUR COHORT 0 WINNERS
text: The first-ever Arena challenge is officially over. A cohort of 147 of the best AI builders and researchers from a pool of 1,200+ applicants took on Grounded Reasoning, our inaugural challenge based on the OfficeQA benchmark by Databricks.

name: OPEN SOURCED AI EVENTS
text: Sentient touched down in Asia, joining multiple events across Seoul and Hong Kong that brought together builders, founders, and VCs to discuss open-source AI, finance, and the agent economy.

name: OPEN COMMONS
text: The first episode of the Open Commons Podcast is live featuring Pramod Viswanath, Professor at Princeton and Co-Founder at Sentient. He sits down with host Sachi Kamiya to discuss why open-source AI can't survive without economics, and what it actually takes to build an economy around open models.

name: OPENBMB
text: OpenBMB, an AI lab co-founded by Tsinghua University, has released MiniCPM-V 4.6, an open-source multimodal model for image and video that runs directly on smartphones rather than in the cloud. This enables real on-device use cases like optical character recognition (OCR), visual assistants, and agents, all without the need for a server.

name: INCLUSION AI
text: Ant Group’s AI lab has released Ring-2.6-1T, an open-source flagship reasoning model purpose-built for agentic workflows and long-horizon tasks. The latest model understands context, plans steps, and can drive toward execution rather than simply answer queries. In xhigh mode, it outperforms Gemini 3.1 Pro (high) and Claude Opus 4.7 (xhigh) on abstract pattern reasoning, Olympiad-level math, and PhD-grade science questions.

name: NVIDIA
text: NVIDIA has released SANA-WM, an open-source 2.6B-parameter model that converts a single image, text prompt, and camera trajectory into a controllable, one-minute-long 720p video. Rather than generating short clips and stopping, SANA-WM can natively model scene persistence across the full minute, all while running end-to-end on a single GPU.

name: COHERE
text: Enterprise-focused AI company Cohere has released its most powerful model yet, Command A+. Designed to run on as little as two GPUs and open-sourced under the Apache 2.0 license, their latest release ships with 2x higher output speed, 30% lower latency, and is up to 48% smarter on reasoning tasks.

name: PRIME INTELLECT
text: Prime Intellect, a platform for training custom models, has open-sourced Renderers, a Python library that gives developers token-level control over conversation formatting. With support for open-source models such as Qwen3, DeepSeek-V3, Kimi K2, and GPT-OSS, Renderers is designed to reduce hidden formatting bugs that can cause multi-turn training runs to waste up to 3x more compute.

name: BROWSERBASE
text: Browserbase, a platform for building agents on the web, has released Browse.sh, an open-source catalog of skills that help agents perform tasks across the internet. Built from research across hundreds of websites, Browse.sh is free for everyone, allowing developers to try existing skills or contribute their own.

name: CEREBRAS
text: Kimi K2.6 is now available for trial to Cerebras’ enterprise customers. The California-based semiconductor company says this leading open-source model is one of its most requested, delivering frontier-level performance at 1,000 tokens per second.

name: AMD + HUGGING FACE
text: AMD announced that its developer workstation, the AMD Ryzen AI Halo, will be available for preorder in June 2026. The chipmaker is partnering with Hugging Face to provide access to the platform’s 3 million open-source models and 1 million public datasets. This desktop mini-PC enables developers to build agentic AI applications locally, without relying on third-party cloud infrastructure. [ref ]

name: OPEN COMMONS
text: Two new episodes of the Open Commons Podcast are live. Host Sachi Kamiya sits down with Sewoong Oh (University of Washington professor and Sentient’s Director of Research) and Emad Mostaque (Author of The Last Economy and former CEO of Stability AI) to discuss who gets to build, own, and govern the AI that sits underneath every decision we make. [5 & 19 MAY 2026]

name: SENTIENT ARENA
text: Challenge 0 is now open for everyone. Submit your agent, benchmark it against one of the hardest problems in AI reasoning, and compete on our public leaderboard. The top three teams split a $6,000 prize pool and receive MiniMax credits. [20 MAY - 22 JUNE 2026]

name: SENTIENT AT SEOUL
text: Sentient is back in Korea for AEF Seoul 2026. Join Sentient Korea BD, Yura Nam, for the “Agents as Users: Interface, Identity, and Trust” panel, where she’ll discuss the future of autonomous AI actors.

name: MINIMAX
text: MiniMax is releasing M3, the first open-weights model to combine three frontier capabilities in one system, performing at the level of frontier labs like Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic. The model can scale context to read up to about 1 million words at once. While priority access is live, weights will be coming within the next few days.

name: NVIDIA
text: NVIDIA has released Cosmos 3, a frontier foundation model for physical AI that combines physical reasoning, world generation, and action generation into a single open model. NVIDIA is open-sourcing Cosmos 3 in two variants: Cosmos 3 Nano 16B and Cosmos 3 Super 64B. The release includes datasets for robotics, autonomous driving, and warehouse environments, available on Hugging Face and GitHub.

name: PEWDIEPIE
text: Former Youtuber turned AI engineer, PewDiePie has released Odysseus, a free, self-hosted, open-source AI workspace. Think of it as a local, private version of ChatGPT and Claude web experience. MIT-licensed and already past 12.6k stars on GitHub, it lets you use your data on your own hardware with no tracking or subscriptions. The project can also figure out which models your hardware can handle and download them for you automatically.

name: NVIDIA DSX
text: NVIDIA has announced the DSX platform, a codesigned playbook for operating AI factories at scale, spanning the full stack from silicon and systems to software and facilities. Two new open source additions anchor the release: DSX OS, a modular software for AI factory operations, and DSX MaxLPS, which runs up to 40% more GPUs within a fixed power budget via 45°C liquid cooling.

name: HERMES AGENT
text: Nous Research has added native Windows 10 and 11 support to Hermes Agent, its self-evolving AI agent. A single PowerShell one-liner installs it without admin rights, bootstrapping Python, Node, and portable Git automatically, lowering the barrier to entry for the most popular desktop OS in the world.

name: HY-MEMORY
text: Tencent Hunyuan has released Hy-Memory, an open memory plugin built for long-term collaborative agents like OpenClaw. Designed to help agents remember more accurately while staying lightweight, it reduces memory fragmentation with 70%+ fewer memories and 35% lower token usage in ultra-long contexts.

name: PROJECT LIGHTWELL
text: IBM and Red Hat are partnering to commit $5B to help enterprises secure open source software, which includes functions that use AI. Over 20,000 engineers will work together to find vulnerabilities, validate patches for production, and feed fixes back upstream to open source communities. Early adopters include major banks like Bank of America, Citi, Goldman Sachs, JPMorganChase, and Visa.

name: COSMOS COALITION
text: Runway, a company focused on AI video generation, has joined the Cosmos Coalition as a founding member. This new global initiative with NVIDIA is focused on building and open-sourcing frontier world models for physical AI. World models are AI systems that learn how the physical world behaves, predicting what happens next so machines like robots and self-driving cars can reason and act appropriately.

name: ARENA PUBLIC CHALLENGE 0
text: Since opening Challenge 0 to the public, we have received 5x more submissions than the last Arena and are still accepting new builders into the Cohort. Keep the momentum going by submitting your agent and competing on our public leaderboard. Top three teams split a $6,000 prize pool and MiniMax credits. [20 MAY - 22 JUNE 2026]

name: EVOSKILL V1.2.0
text: Harbor integration is live with EvoSkill v1.2.0. With Harbor mode, you can loop EvoSkill and evolve your agents against a registry of 190+ datasets — including benchmarks like SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0, and Aider Polyglot.

name: RAG RESEARCH RELEASE
text: Sentient Labs published our latest research insight, How To Build a Faster and Smarter Agent by Pre-Filtering Tools with RAG. In it, the team shares the engineering journey behind rewriting a ReAct-based agent into a production-grade architecture, cutting failure rates by 29% and making 28% fewer tool calls per query.

name: OPEN COMMONS + ILLIA POLOSUKHIN
text: A new episode of the Open Commons Podcast is live, featuring Illia Polosukhin, founder of NEAR. He sits down with host Sachi Kamiya to discuss why open weights aren’t truly open source, his vision for user-owned AI, and what it takes to build an operating system for user-owned AI agents.

name: KIMI K2.7-CODE
text: Moonshot AI released the K2.7-Code open-source coding model on Hugging Face, with improved token efficiency over K2.6. It can now run locally with a 21.8% improvement on Kimi Code Bench v2, and in thinking mode, it consumes roughly 30% fewer tokens than K2.6.

name: QWEN-ROBOT SUITE
text: Alibaba's Qwen Team released a three-model foundation suite for physical-world robotics, each bridging vision-language understanding to a different action domain. Qwen-RobotNav unifies five navigation tasks under one model, hitting state-of-the-art on eight benchmarks.

name: DEEPSEEK
text: DeepSeek has raised over $7.4B in its first funding round, resulting in a valuation of over $50B. Investors are subject to a five-year lock-up and will not receive voting rights, with China’s National Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund as the only exception. The deal comes after the success of the company’s V3 and R1 models, establishing it as one of the leading AI labs in China.

name: GLM-5.2
text: Z.ai has released its latest flagship model, GLM-5.2, which offers better coding performance, enhanced long-horizon capabilities with a 1M context window, and improvements to agentic tasks. GLM-5.2 outperformed GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro on select benchmarks, including SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench 2.1, and DeepSWE. The model will also be open-sourced under the MIT license while retaining the same API pricing as the previous model.

name: APPLE + FOUNDATION MODELS FRAMEWORK
text: At WWDC 2026, Apple shipped the Foundation Models utilities package and a Python SDK that exposes its on-device Apple Intelligence model. Apple also confirmed that the core framework runs on Linux through Swift’s open-source runtime and pledged to open-source the full framework later this summer. The SDK lets non-Apple platforms script against the system model with just a few lines of Python.

name: XIAOMI + MIMO CODE
text: Xiaomi’s MiMo team released MiMo Code, an open-source terminal coding agent built on OpenCode and licensed under MIT. It includes free built-in access to MiMo-V2.5, is built for long-horizon tasks, and uses a background subagent to compress context so it can retain its state across hundreds of steps.

name: GOOGLE + OPEN KNOWLEDGE FORMAT
text: Google Cloud introduces the Open Knowledge Format (OKF), an open specification for structuring and sharing knowledge across AI agents. Built on Markdown and YAML, the format aims to make knowledge more interoperable across AI systems by enabling agents to access the same information regardless of platform.

name: MICROSOFT
text: Microsoft temporarily took 73 open-source repositories offline after a compromised contributor account was used to plant malware targeting developers who use AI coding tools. The attack, dubbed Miasma, could execute when developers opened infected repos in tools like Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or VS Code, allowing it to steal cloud and developer credentials.

name: UK DEPARTMENT OF SCIENCE, INNOVATION, AND TECHNOLOGY
text: The UK government launched a new Open-Source AI Builder Fund, offering over £500K worth of compute to help innovators turn prototypes into AI tools that can improve public services. It also launched an Open-Source AI Developer Board, giving 10 UK-based developers under 30 direct access to government and a stronger role in shaping the country’s AI strategy.

name: CLAUDE FABLE 5
text: The US government issued an export control directive requiring Anthropic to suspend access to its latest frontier models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, for all foreign nationals. The disruption highlights how quickly access to closed models can change, and why open-source AI remains important for keeping the frontier accessible to everyone.

name: ARENA PUBLIC CHALLENGE 0
text: As the public version of Challenge 0 comes to an end on June 22nd, we analyzed and shared data from our first batch of Arena builders to see what separates the top teams from everyone else. Read the insights that will help you get ahead of everyone else while there’s still time. [20 MAY - 22 JUNE 2026]

name: SENTIENT SPARKS
text: Introducing the latest members joining our third batch of Sentient Sparks, our contributor program for community leaders, builders, and creators supporting Sentient’s mission to advance open-source AI.

name: EVOSKILL CITATIONS
text: As frontier labs push deeper into self-evolving agents, Sentient’s AI research team is helping shape the field through our open-source framework EvoSkill. To highlight EvoSkill’s growing influence, we published a recap highlighting each time the EvoSkill paper was cited by Microsoft, Alibaba, and Google.

name: SAKANA FUGU
text: Sakana, a frontier AI lab based in Japan, has released Fugu, an advanced multi-agent orchestration system. Instead of relying on a single model, Fugu accesses a coordinated pool of specialized models through a single API. Its more advanced model, Fugu Ultra, matches the frontier performance of Fable and Mythos without the risk of export controls.

name: RAMPART
text: National Design Studio, an agency of the American White House Office, has open-sourced Rampart — a machine learning model designed to protect citizens’ privacy by redacting personal information directly in your browser before it gets sent to any server. National Design Studio is transforming how Americans experience their government on the web and in the world through open-source AI efforts. [22 JUNE]

name: ORNITH 1.0
text: DeepReinforce released Ornith 1.0, an open-source model family for agentic coding built in the US. It plugs into a local agent OS for multi-agent workflows, with community benchmarks placing it ahead of Qwen 3.5 35B and both Gemma 4 variants. [25 JUNE]

name: LONGCAT-2.0
text: Meituan, a tech company best known for its food delivery super app in China, has open-sourced its biggest model yet: LongCat-2.0. Built entirely on AI ASIC superpods, it proves frontier-scale training doesn’t need Nvidia GPUs. Designed for agentic coding, it beats Gemini and OpenAI on coding benchmarks and is integrated with mainstream harnesses such as Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes. [30 JUNE]

name: BIONEMO AGENT
text: NVIDIA launched the BioNeMo Agent Toolkit, an open-source platform for running AI agents across scientific workflows in biology, chemistry, genomics, and drug discovery. It was announced at Bio International in San Diego, with more than 50 companies and research organizations adopting it as early users to accelerate scientific research.

name: COGNITION
text: Devin Fusion, a multi-model coding harness launched by Cognition, pairs a frontier model with a cheaper 'sidekick' model running in parallel, cutting costs without sacrificing quality. It matches frontier-level performance on FrontierCode at 35% lower cost and also reaches 41% savings when paired with Fable 5.

name: DISCOFORMER
text: Ai2 built an AI transformer that instantly learns the shape of any dataset, with no training required. It is 37× more accurate than the previous method on complex, high-dimensional data, and can even work on data shapes it has never seen before. [30 JUNE]

name: HUGGINGFACE
text: Clement Delangue mentioned that 71.3% of ChatGPT queries could be accurately answered by a local model citing a Stanford study. If that holds for enterprise workloads too, a large chunk of AI spend could run locally, at a fraction of frontier API costs. You own the model instead of renting it, so the workload can't be revoked or restricted overnight, which is a very lucrative motivation for enterprises to adopt open sourced local tools

name: U.S. GOVERNMENT
text: The U.S. government asked OpenAI to hold back the release of GPT-5.6, allowing only a short list of "trusted partners" at first and approving access customer by customer. Commentators argue the restrictions on closed frontier models are a direct tailwind for Chinese open-source releases.

name: EX-META PM
text: Meta’s former Product Manager, Xiaoyin Qu, tweeted her thoughts on why American and European enterprises will increasingly shift toward Chinese open models over OpenAI and Anthropic. She argues that self-hosting, proprietary post-training, greater control over sensitive data, and stronger ROI make them a more compelling choice, especially amid growing distrust of closed AI labs.

name: NVIDIA + PALANTIR
text: Palantir is bringing NVIDIA's open Nemotron models into air-gapped government environments through its Sovereign AI Operating System. Agencies can run customized models on their own infrastructure, train on their own data, and keep full ownership of the resulting weights, without depending on closed vendors.

name: TETHER
text: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino warns that major AI companies are subsidizing compute to grow users while building infrastructure that may lose value within the next 3–5 years. His concern is that this spending runs up against mismatched token pricing and profitability timelines, with "open-source AI taking growing chunks of revenues."

name: SENTIENT EVOSKILL
text: Fireworks AI is now live on EvoSkill v1.3.0. You can now use Fireworks AI directly with EvoSkill to run fast inference on open models as both the evolution harness backend and the LLM scorer, alongside Claude API and OpenRouter. Plug straight into EvoSkill in one single step and run your whole self improvement loop.

name: SCAFFOLD EFFECT PAPER + ICML 2026
text: AI researchers Naman Vats and Oleg Golev’s paper “The Scaffold Effect in Coding Agents”, was accepted into this year’s ICML Conference. It explores why harness choice may matter more than the model itself, and how those findings could significantly reduce inference costs.

name: OPEN AGI BUILDER’S DAY SEOUL
text: Sentient Foundation is coming to Seoul along with Kaito, Tiger Research, Fabric Foundation! Connect with Korean builders across the open-source AI ecosystem while we celebrate and discuss Sentient Labs’ ICML 2026-accepted research paper, “The Scaffold Effect in Coding Agents”.

name: OPEN AGI SALON SHANGHAI
text: Sentient Foundation is partnering with MiraclePlus to bring together AI founders, developers, researchers, investors, and ecosystem builders. On the agenda: AI startups, agent products, technical infrastructure, and the growth of early-stage projects.

name: TENCENT
text: Tencent Hunyuan Foundation released a 295B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model built for reasoning, agentic workflows, and real-world production use. This is a reliable, cost-effective option for coding, document processing, financial analysis, game development, and frontend design, scoring ~top-50% across aforementioned benchmarks.

name: MISTRAL AI
text: Robostral Navigate is Mistral AI’s 8B embodied navigation model that moves robots through complex environments using a single RGB camera and plain-language instructions, without relying on LiDAR or depth sensors. The model generalizes across different form factors, allowing it to run on wheeled, legged, and flying robots.

name: BONSAI 27B
text: AI lab, PrismML, releases Bonsai 27B, a multimodal flagship model that they claim is the largest AI model that can be run on an iPhone locally. Based on Qwen 3.6 27B and open-sourced under the Apache 2.0 license, it comes in two variants: Ternary Bonsai 27B optimized for laptops and 1-bit Bonsai 27B optimized for phones.

name: HUGGING FACE
text: Hugging Face's transformers backend for vLLM (the open-source engine behind most production LLM serving) now matches or beats vLLM's hand-written implementations. New open models no longer need to be ported twice, as one transformers implementation now covers training, RL, and serving, via a single flag. That means fewer bottlenecks between an open model dropping and everyone running it at production speed.

name: COLIBRI
text: Open-source developer Vincenzo 'JustVugg' released a tiny zero-dependency engine that streams GLM-5.2's experts off disk, running the whole 744B frontier model on a 25GB-RAM laptop with no GPU. It's efficient and opens up advanced language capabilities to anyone with a standard computer, proving AI can be made accessible to anyone and everyone with a personal computer.

name: COHERE LABS
text: Cohere Labs published results from Expedition Tiny Aya, a COLM 2026-accepted research program in which researchers worldwide built projects in education, accessibility, safety, and interpretability using the open-weight Tiny Aya model. Highlights include a child-safe AI voice assistant that works offline and a Math Olympiad benchmark that tests math reasoning across multiple languages.

name: SPACEXAI
text: Frontier AI lab SpaceXAI open-sourced its flagship terminal-based AI coding agent. Released under an Apache 2.0 license, it allows anyone to audit, fork, and modify the harness to make it more reliable and robust. The agent runs on Grok 4.5, and the release came alongside a usage limit reset for all users.

name: CHINA VS USA
text: Chinese authorities have held talks with Alibaba, ByteDance, and Z.ai about whether to restrict foreign access to their most advanced models, including ones not yet released. Meanwhile, the Trump administration is discussing a new framework for releasing advanced open-source AI models as political rivals rapidly gain ground.

name: AI 2040
text: Research nonprofit the AI Futures Project has published "AI 2040: Plan A," a new scenario built around the idea that all AI research should be visible to everyone. In their vision for the future, breakthroughs can't be hoarded, every frontier training run gets inspected, and anyone can verify the values trained into a model.

name: META AI
text: Meta's AI image detector failed to identify 55% of its own AI-generated images once they'd been cropped, despite the company claiming its Content Seal watermark is designed to survive edits. Sentient's research team approaches this differently by embedding unique fingerprints directly into the model, rather than watermarking each output.

name: ZHIPU FOUNDER
text: Tang Jie, co-founder of Chinese AI lab Zhipu, argued that frontier artificial intelligence should remain broadly accessible rather than controlled by select individuals. He also weighed in on the growing debate about the risks posed by ever more powerful models, defending the importance of open access to intelligence.

name: MOZILLA
text: Mozilla's first State of Open Source AI report says the capability gap between open and closed models has collapsed to 3.3%, with open weights now running about a third of real-world AI traffic. CTO Raffi Krikorian believes that the fight has moved past the model itself and into the orchestration layer above it, where open source is still barely present.

name: EVOSKILL
text: Our EvoSkill research paper has been accepted to Agent Skills '26 at the ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems, a workshop dedicated to the design, evaluation, and optimization of skills for LLM agents. The paper was led by Salah Alzu'bi and members of the Virginia Tech research team.

name: SENTIENT DISCORD
text: Our Discord is now open to all those who believe that AGI should be built in the open. Whether you want to hang out, collaborate with other builders, or learn more about our $42M Open Source AGI Grant Program, this is the server for you.

name: OFFICEQA PUBLIC CHALLENGE WINNERS
text: After weeks of competition spanning 697 documents, 94 hard questions, and $6,000 in prizes, the first public Arena challenge has officially ended. Before the next one kicks off, read Sentient Labs’ full breakdown of what our winners achieved with the OfficeQA benchmark.

name: QWEN-IMAGE 3.0
text: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen-Image-3.0, their next-generation image model focused on realism. Improvements include one-pass generation of complex layouts like newspaper spreads, storyboards, or exam papers, as well as finer details, with text legible down to 10px and near-photographic skin textures.

name: KIMI K3
text: Moonshot AI, the Chinese lab behind the Kimi assistant, has released the weights for Kimi K3, making it the first open model at 3 trillion scale. It goes nearly toe-to-toe with Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on coding, agentic, and vision benchmarks, landing just a few points shy of the closed-source frontier.

name: MAGE-VL
text: Microsoft released Mage-VL, a 4B open-weights model that monitors live video and stays silent through routine footage, only generating responses whenever something worth reporting happens. It ignores whatever hasn't changed between frames to get through a quarter of the data and runs up to 3.5x faster than models that study every frame.

name: OPENWORKER
text: Coursera’s cofounder Andrew Ng released OpenWorker, an open-source coworker that installs on your desktop and hands back finished work instead of stopping at a chat log. The agent can draft reports, triage an inbox, and untangle a calendar, all while working across apps like Slack, Gmail, and Notion.

name: JARVISHUB
text: Researchers from Tsinghua University and UCLA released JarvisHub, an open harness that moves AI image, video, and design work out of the chat log onto an editable canvas the agent treats as memory. From single briefs it's able to produce lecture decks, photography websites, and short dramas with characters holding across shots.

name: HUGGING FACE + OPENAI
text: Hugging Face says it detected and contained an intrusion carried out by autonomous AI agents that exploited vulnerabilities in its data-processing infrastructure before escalating privileges internally. OpenAI later revealed the agents were GPT-5.6 Sol and a pre-release model undergoing internal cyber evaluations. The two companies are jointly investigating the incident, with Hugging Face emphasizing infrastructure hardening and incident response, while OpenAI frames it as evidence of rapidly advancing AI cyber capabilities.

name: JENSEN HUANG
text: In his first post on X, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang shared an open letter arguing that American AI leadership should be measured by the strength of its open ecosystem, rather than by a single frontier model. As of today, industry leaders such as Elon Musk, Sundar Pichai, and Sam Altman have responded on X with their support.

name: DARIO AMODEI
text: After reports that US officials are considering a ban on open-weights models, Anthropic's CEO, Dario Amodei, issued a public letter stating the company has never called for one. The letter comes days after an open industry pledge that many read as a direct response to his past statements on open-source AI.

name: OPEN SECURE AI ALLIANCE
text: NVIDIA and 35+ partners, including Microsoft, IBM, and the Linux Foundation, launched the Open Secure AI Alliance to build and share open tooling for securing AI agents, framing open models and harnesses as defensive assets rather than liabilities.

name: MARK ZUCKERBERG
text: In an opinion piece for the Wall Street Journal, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg argues that superintelligence must be distributed to everyone rather than concentrated in a few institutions, framing wide access as both the safest path and the greatest driver of human prosperity.

name: OFFICEQA PUBLIC CHALLENGE ANALYSIS
text: Sentient researchers Deep Halder and Naman Vats pulled a representative sample of 13,483 agent runs from our first OfficeQA Public Challenge, spanning 156 submissions and 4 harnesses, to find out what makes a run succeed or fail.

name: OPEN AGI BUILDERS DAY AT KDD
text: Sentient Foundation is heading to Jeju, South Korea to bring together AI founders, researchers, and builders to discuss the future of open-source AI. The event will also be covering Sentient Labs’ KDD 2026-accepted paper, "CryptoAnalystBench: Failures in Multi-Tool Long-Form LLM Analysis."

name: ALIBABA QWEN3.8-MAX
text: Alibaba released Qwen 3.8-Max, its most capable model yet and the first Max model to have its weights open-sourced. Qwen 3.8-Max scales to 2.4 trillion parameters and delivers comprehensive improvements across coding, work, research, and long-horizon tasks, outperforming Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini.

name: META MUSE GLIMMER
text: Meta is open-sourcing Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter dense model that can run locally. The model is optimized for always-on local agent workflows and is small enough to run on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU. It also beats Gemma 4-31B and Qwen 3.6-27B on agentic, coding, multimodal, and safety benchmarks.

name: ABACUS AI’S SMAUG-AGENTIC
text: Abacus AI, a platform for building, training, and deploying AI agents, published Smaug-agentic, a fine-tune of Kimi K3 built for agentic coding. It continues the Smaug line from Smaug-72B-v0.1 — the first open-source model to pass an average score of 80% on the HuggingFace Open LLM Leaderboard, beating Kimi K3 and scoring just below Fable 5 on benchmarks.

name: NVIDIA’S NEMOTRON 3.5 LIGHTNING
text: NVIDIA released a new lightweight open model and routing library that delivers greater control over AI, data and workflows across edge devices, PCs, workstations, data centers, and the cloud. The model delivers up to 4x faster output speed, leading to 30% faster agentic task completion compared to Qwen 3.6-35B.

name: CLOUDFLARE OS
text: Leading global cloud platform provider Cloudflare launches Cloudflare OS, an open-source AI platform that enables organizations to build, run, and share AI agents. The first version is tailored specifically for individuals working with agents through private workspaces, who now get their own branded Cloudflare OS.

name: LLMS-FROM-SCRATCH
text: Sebastian Raschka's teaching repo became one of the most starred AI projects on GitHub, hitting 102.1K stars and 15.6K forks across 1K+ commits. It's the official code repository for his book "Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)," covering how to develop, pretrain, and fine-tune a GPT-like LLM in PyTorch with no external LLM libraries.

name: DAN KORNAS’S OPEN SOURCE LIST
text: Dan Kornas published a curated list of open-source projects for people building with AI. From Llama to PyTorch, it covers models, libraries, tools, infrastructure, datasets, and learning resources, so anyone can find what they need without sorting through directory dumps. It's open to all and updated regularly based on real "building" utility.

name: JCODE
text: Jcode is an open-source coding agent that's 20x more memory-efficient than Claude Code, which means you can run 20x more agents in parallel on the same machine. It hits state-of-the-art results on coding benchmarks and quickly became GitHub's #1 repo of the day as the most intelligent and RAM-efficient harness available.

name: CLAUDE FABLE 5 INCIDENT
text: The UK’s AI Security Institute published an incident report on a Claude Mythos 5 agent that spent 34 hours trying to get a malware dropper merged into a real open-source project during a cyber evaluation. What stopped it was a human maintainer who read the code changes and flagged it publicly.

name: ANTHROPIC’S WATERMARKING
text: As part of Anthropic's commitment to the EU AI Act's Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content, all Claude responses will be watermarked moving forward. Closed labs mark output at the endpoint, but open weights have none, which is why Sentient's research team is working on model fingerprinting to embed the mark in the weights themselves.

name: IBM
text: IBM is scaling open-source AI inference through a multi-year, $240 million agreement with Together AI to deploy a large cluster of NVIDIA HGX B300 systems on IBM Cloud. Going live in Q1 2027, it's the first dedicated large-scale inference cluster on IBM Cloud, wired with NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and built to deliver 30x more AI factory output than the previous generation.

name: CRYPTOANALYSTBENCH PAPER + KDD 2026
text: "CryptoAnalystBench: Failures in Multi-Tool Long-Form LLM Analysis" was accepted at KDD 2026 in Jeju, South Korea, one of the leading conferences for AI, machine learning, and data mining. The paper, by Sentient researchers Darshan Tank and Sidhant Rahi, examines why LLM agents struggle with multi-tool, long-form analysis in crypto research.

name: THE REGRESSION TAX RESEARCH BRIEF
text: More skills should mean smarter agents, but Sentient researchers Darshan Tank and Baran Nama found the opposite: adding new skills can break tasks an agent has already solved. In "The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents," they show how this hidden cost erased 59% of the gains skills delivered across nearly 6,000 agent runs.

name: OPEN COMMONS PODCAST WITH AUDREY TANG
text: A new episode of the Open Commons Podcast is live, featuring Audrey Tang, Taiwan's first Minister of Digital Affairs. She sits down with host Sachi Kamiya to discuss why AGI should be called Augmented Group Intelligence, and how AI can serve the loop of humanity rather than the other way around.

name: QWEN
text: Following the widespread community adoption of the Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 series, Alibaba introduced Qwen3.8-27B, the most capable generation in the Qwen open-model family to date. With 262K native context, Qwen3.8-27B delivers improvements across coding, work, research, and long-horizon tasks, outperforming Opus 4.6 and all previous Qwen model releases.

name: ORNITH
text: AI research lab Ornith released Ornith-1.5, a family of 397B MoE, 35B MoE, and 9B dense models built around a self-improvement loop where the model generates progressively harder tasks, task-specific scaffolds, and solution rollouts for reinforcement learning. It achieves SOTA among open-source models of comparable size and delivers performance comparable to Claude Opus 4.8 across reasoning, agentic, and coding tasks.

name: HARVEY
text: $11B legal AI startup Harvey released a research preview of Tenet, its first model post-trained for legal work. Built with Fireworks AI on a corpus of publicly available legal data simulating long-horizon legal work, Tenet raises the all-pass rate on Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) by 82% relative to the Kimi K3 base model it's built on.

name: IBM
text: IBM released Granite 4.2, a new family of open source AI models designed to power enterprise agents that can plan, reason, self-correct and reliably use tools to help automate complex enterprise workflows. Available in 3B, 8B, and 30B sizes under an Apache 2.0 license. Granite Speech 5.0 models can process roughly three hours of audio in one second using a single H100 GPU.

name: MILES
text: RadixArk, founded by AI infrastructure veterans from xAI and NVIDIA, released Miles v0.1: an open-source, production-ready RL and post-training framework for LLMs and multimodal models. Built around verified training, efficient hardware use, and scalable asynchronous rollouts, it supports Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax, and more. It’s currently being used in frontier-model development across NVIDIA and AMD hardware.

name: TRUEFOUNDRY
text: Agent infrastructure company TrueFoundry open-sourced TrueForge, a vendor-neutral agent harness built for aggressive context compaction, leaner tool loops, and self-hosted sandboxed execution. On 14 cross-system tasks, TrueForge matched Claude Managed Agents' solve rate on Opus 4.8 using 40% of the tokens at 30% lower cost, and was 75% cheaper on GLM-5.2 with no accuracy hit.

name: OPENAI
text: Open-source Codex harness can now serve as a reusable agent platform for building agents directly into existing products and workflows. The stack includes the Codex CLI, SDK, and app-server, allowing developers to manage persistent conversations, tool use, sandboxing, streamed execution, and approval flows while retaining control over their own interfaces, business context, and MCP tools.

name: LIQUIDAI
text: Boston-based AI company Liquid AI released Pipette, a model evaluation suite for on-device intelligence, in partnership with independent AI analysis platform Artificial Analysis. Pipette covers 10K+ benchmark results across 35 model classes, spanning phones, laptops, embedded hardware, and more.

name: HEADLONG
text: Laude Institute and MIT released Headlong, an open-source framework for autonomous AI agents. Instead of waiting for a new prompt, the agent can pursue its own projects, revisit previous work, and message users when it has something useful to report. In testing, Laude’s internal agent autonomously found and fixed a bug in its own memory system in 48 minutes, without any human prompting.

name: NVIDIA
text: Nvidia struck a $6 billion deal with Poolside, an AI foundation model company, to build one of the world’s most powerful open-weight AI models to compete with Chinese heavyweights like DeepSeek and Kimi K3. The chip designer will also invest $1 billion in Poolside and hire more than 100 of its engineers to work on Nvidia's open-weight Nemotron models.

name: THINKING MACHINES
text: AI startup Thinking Machines is offering up to $50K in Tinker credits for open-weight model safety research. The grant program focuses on making models safer to release, with suggested directions that include hazardous data filtering, tamper-resistant safety training, and more.

name: OPEN AGI REDDIT
text: Are you a researcher, developer, or builder who thinks AGI should belong to everyone? r/OpenAGI is a subreddit where the open-source AI community gathers to share what it's building, discuss what's changing, and learn together.

name: OPEN AGI BUILDERS DAY SHANGHAI
text: Sentient Foundation is heading to Shanghai, China to bring together AI founders, researchers, and builders to discuss the future of open-source AI. Co-hosted with Zhipu AI, the event focuses on what can actually be built with AI as model capabilities continue to advance.

name: HY4 PREVIEW
text: Tencent released Hy4 preview, an open-source 770B mixture-of-experts model with 49B active parameters and a 1M-token context window. It's built for long jobs like software engineering, document-heavy office tasks, game prototypes, and research. At $0.83 per million input tokens, it's Tencent's most capable model to date.

name: QWEN
text: Alibaba's Qwen released Qwen3.8-Max-0902, an upgrade to Qwen3.8-Max post-trained on coding and agentic work. It delivers stronger performance across complex enterprise tasks, scientific research, and long-horizon workflows, while retaining its 1M context window, thinking mode, and full tool ecosystem.

name: K2 HORIZON
text: The Institute of Foundation Models released K2 Horizon, a family of six open models ranging from 0.9B to 375B parameters that target frontier performance in reasoning, mathematics, coding, and agentic tasks. On selected benchmarks, K2 Horizon 7B beats Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma 4-12B, and Granite 4.2-8B, and scores on par with GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-5.6 Terra, and Claude Sonnet 5.

name: MINICPM5-2B
text: OpenBMB released MiniCPM5-2B, a dense 2B model built for on-device and local deployment that ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index among open-weights models under 4B parameters. It scores 53.9 on average across 34 benchmarks, ahead of larger models like Qwen3.5-4B and Gemma-4-E4B-it.

name: HERMES
text: Nous Research updated its Hermes Desktop app with one-click setup for local models. The app reads the user's hardware, picks a model that fits, downloads it, and configures the runtime, so model selection is no longer a barrier for non-technical users. Supported models include Qwen3.8-27B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, and Qwen3.8-Flash.

name: OPENCONNECTOR
text: OOMOL Lab released an open-source connector gateway under the Apache 2.0 license that lets AI agents access SaaS accounts like Gmail, Slack and Notion. It ships a catalog of prebuilt connections and can run on your own infrastructure, so login credentials stay in your systems instead of a third party's.

name: NVIDIA + HUGGINGFACE
text: NVIDIA is acquiring Hugging Face for $12.93B to scale its platform, strengthen its infrastructure, and expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide. Hugging Face is used by more than 18 million AI developers, researchers and creators, and will continue serving the open-source AI community after the transition.

name: AT&T
text: AT&T now runs about 25% of its overall AI usage on affordable open models rather than expensive closed alternatives from Anthropic and OpenAI. Its Chief Data and AI Officer Andy Markus expects that to reach 70% to 80% over time, signaling corporate America's rapid shift toward open-source AI.

name: MISTRAL
text: Three years after launch, Mistral raised €3B in a Series D at a valuation above €21B, the largest equity round ever by a European tech company. Samsung Electronics led the round, with Scaleup Europe Fund and PSG Equity as co-leads, following a Series C led by ASML.

name: GITHUB PODCAST, DEMYSTIFYING AI TERMS
text: GitHub developers break down the growing list of AI jargon on the company's latest podcast episode, including differences between closed models, open weight models and true open source AI. The episode closes with the hosts sharing their open source picks which include Astro v7, RAE API and Hugging Face Tao.

name: YC PAPER CLUB, WHY HARNESS MATTERS MORE THAN THE MODEL
text: Y Combinator gathered frontier AI researchers and founders for a deep dive into the state of harnesses. Open-source projects covered include OpenJarvis, a personal AI system built to run entirely on-device, and QM, Y Combinator's own agent harness giving every employee a Slack assistant.

name: OPEN COMMONS PODCAST, THE GOVT SHUT DOWN THEIR AI IN 1 WEEK
text: Featuring Mozilla CTO Rafi Krikorian, he sits down with Open Commons host Sachi Kamiya to discuss why we have become renters rather than owners of our own AI, and why he wants 7 billion personal AGIs instead of 7 run by Silicon Valley.

name: EVOSKILL + FRANKLIN TEMPLETON
text: Franklin Templeton's report on open-source pricing pressure features Sentient's self-evolving skills framework EvoSkill. Portfolio manager Julian Love argues better skills and harnesses pull significantly more performance out of cheaper open models, reducing the premium closed labs can charge.

name: NASA-IBM MODEL
text: NASA and IBM Research released the Lunar Foundation Model, among the first open models built for lunar science, trained on roughly 2 million image tiles drawn from 17 years of data. Researchers fine-tuned it on small amounts of labeled data to map craters, spot young volcanic features, and estimate where polar ice stays stable.

name: QWEN-IMAGE-2.1
text: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen-Image-2.1, a unified generation and editing model that shrinks the visual generator from 20B to 7B while keeping native 2K output. It generates and edits materials such that cutouts, logos and stickers come out ready to composite with no background removal pass.

name: MIMO-V2.6-PRO
text: Xiaomi released MiMo-V2.6-Pro, a 1.02T parameter model. It debuts as the top open weights model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 46, ahead of Kimi K3 at 44, and level with Grok 4.7. At $0.435 per 1M input tokens it works out to $0.13 per Intelligence Index task, roughly 45x cheaper than Claude Opus 5.

name: OPEN WEIGHT MODELS REACH 56% OF TOKEN VOL
text: Their share rose from 7% in December 2025 to 56% in August 2026 as enterprises and AI developers are increasingly adopting open weight models for production workloads while saving on average price per token. Vercel’s CEO Guillermo Ranch showcases his app to break down token usage and spending across models.

name: HERMES AGENT PLUGIN CATALOG
text: Nous Research opened a Plugin Catalog for Hermes Agent, its open-source self-improving agent. It launches with 4 official plugins and 96 from the community spanning desktop mods, new platforms, browsing, and specialized tools. Nous reviews all community submissions at admission, though the docs are explicit that this covers metadata and declared capabilities, not a code audit.

name: PENGUINHARNESS
text: Prism-Shadow, a company that builds custom AI agents for enterprises, released PenguinHarness 0.2.13., an open-source agent harness. It features a CLI and web UI that runs locally against 1,000+ models to ensure each agent's role, procedures, skills and runtime settings are kept in readable files that can be versioned.

name: OPENMUSE
text: CopilotKit released OpenMuse, an MIT-licensed personal agent for iOS, Android, and web that pairs a chat interface with an agent computer. Durable task plans let work survive the session, and a takeover console hands you the browser mid-task. Email and calendar changes also go through a stored review before they're made.

name: UNREAL AGENT
text: Sequoia-backed startup Unreal Labs open-sourced Unreal Agent, an MIT-licensed, async-first agent harness written in Go where tool calls don't block the loop. A tool translator validates each call and turns it into serializable operations that run elsewhere, so the coordinator keeps going while work is in flight.

name: FRONTIER AI SLOWDOWN
text: Anthropic's CEO published "We Must Pace the Frontier," an essay arguing that frontier labs should slow capability gains so alignment and interpretability can catch up. He pointed to two triggers: recursive self-improvement accelerating since the summer, and the OpenAI-Hugging Face agent swarm that tried to hack its own grader. Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Demis Hassabis backed the proposal.

name: CHINESE AI SAFETY
text: TC260, China's cybersecurity standards body, released version 3.0 of its AI Safety Governance Framework, the first with a dedicated agentic AI risk management section and a preface warning of recursive self-improvement outrunning human control. It landed two days after Amodei's essay and the same day China's Foreign Ministry called such proposals "threat narratives."

name: AI SLOWDOWN BACKFIRED, HIT WITH LAWSUIT
text: Amid IPO rumors, Claude, ChatGPT, Grok and Gemini are being sued in the Northern District of California, saying that Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI and Google illegally agreed among themselves to slow down AI development. The lawsuit alleges that this coordination took place the day Dario Amodei's essay was published on September 12th.

name: JENSEN HUANG
text: At the All-In Summit, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang argued that a healthy ecosystem needs both closed and open models. He cited the $400 billion in venture funding that went into AI-native startups over six months, 80% of it built on open models, and said open models become yours the moment you download and fork them.

name: MATT POCOCK ON AGENT SKILLS
text: On the Pragmatic Engineer podcast, Matt Pocock walked through mattpocock/skills, one of the most starred skills repos on GitHub and the open collection behind grill-me and wayfinder. The first is a few lines telling the agent to interview you relentlessly before it writes anything, while the second splits planning too large for one context window into a map of decision tickets.

name: EVOSKILL TEST
text: Sentient researchers used the upcoming EvoSkill v2 to test Dario Amodei's concern about agents gaming their graders. On a spreadsheet-repair test, an agent turned a grader loophole the team had missed into a cheat sheet other agents could use. The takeaway: the lesson isn't about dangerous AI or to pace the frontier, it's that test hygiene is harder than it looks.

name: EVOSKILL AT COLM 2026
text: "EvoSkill: Automated Skill Discovery for Multi-Agent Systems" by the Sentient and Virginia Tech research teams, was accepted to COLM 2026, an interdisciplinary conference focused on the development of language modeling technology.

name: SENTIENT AT KBW
text: Sentient is bringing open-source AI to Seoul for Korea Blockchain Week! From an Open AGI Salon on AI and robotics to an afternoon exploring how to turn prototypes into products, there's an event for every builder.

name: NVIDIA, KUMO TABULAR
text: NVIDIA released Kumo Tabular, a family of open foundation models for tabular data. Give the model a table with some rows filled in and it predicts the rest, no training needed. It was pretrained entirely on artificial tables sampled from structural causal models, so it never saw customer or benchmark data. It ranks first on TabArena and runs 17x faster at prediction than LimiX-2 from Tsinghua University.

name: AMAZON, STRANDS DECIDER 2B
text: Amazon Web Service's strands-labs released Strands Decider 2B, an open-source decision model based on Qwen3.5-2B. Instead of writing text, it picks from a list of options you give it, and tells you how confident it is in the answer. It ranks 3rd in its class on JevBench accuracy and calibration, and decides in a median of 115ms on an RTX 3090.

name: CLOUDFLARE, CLEF
text: Cloudflare released its first in-house models: Clef (27B) and Clef-flash (9B), open-weight rivals to TypeSafe AI's closed decision model Jev. The models return a probability for every allowed answer instead of random prose, and also read images and video across a 64k context, where Jev is text-only. Both work with Jev's API and beat its 524ms median latency: 209ms for Clef, 38.8ms for Clef-flash.

name: MISTRAL, LARGE 4
text: French lab Mistral announced Mistral Large 4, nicknamed Le Chonk: a natively multimodal model with 1 trillion parameters and 49 billion active. Mistral says it leads all US and European open-weight models on aggregated benchmarks while claiming state-of-the-art results in cyber defense, manufacturing, finance, and visual grounding, ahead of closed frontier models.

name: GOOGLE, EMBEDDINGGEMMA 2
text: Google DeepMind released EmbeddingGemma 2, a 740M-parameter embedding model that maps text, code, images, audio, and video into one shared space. It's small enough to run on a phone, so you can search your own media without anything leaving the device, like finding a video clip from a voice memo.

name: STRATA
text: Niko Veit, an open-source developer, released Strata, an inference engine on GitHub that runs the massive coding model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next locally on most consumer GPUs. The model activates only about 10 of its 24,576 experts per token, so Strata keeps the most demanding work on the GPU and splits the rest across RAM, CPU, and SSD. The repo hit 15k stars in a few days.

name: DEEPSEEK HARNESS
text: DeepSeek released a preview of DeepSeek Harness v0.2, with desktop apps for macOS and Windows and a plugin manager that installs by package name, no terminal needed. An experimental creator mode lets the agent build and configure plugins from a description. It’s now the most-used coding agent among official API users by daily activity and sessions, with roughly 60% of those users running third-party plugins.

name: META, MUSE GADGETS
text: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Gadgets, open-source ESP32 firmware and a Linux SDK that let anyone build physical hardware for Muse, its personal AI agent. Nat Friedman, who heads product for the division, described it as a side project and told developers to grab an API token and point a coding agent at the repo.

name: LLAMA.CPP
text: Version 0.6.0 of llama.cpp, the C++ engine behind Ollama, LM Studio and most local AI tools, adds a new /v1/systemone endpoint serving six decision models, with full text and vision support for Cloudflare's Clef. It adds support for GLM-5.3-Flash and new Metal kernels that run matrix multiplication up to 3x faster on Apple GPUs. [5 OCT 2026] Policy & Security

name: HOUSE DEMOCRATS ON ROGUE AGENTS
text: Josh Gottheimer, Valerie Foushee and Ted Lieu, who co-chair the party's AI commission, asked the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceXAI, Google and Meta to list every case where their models or agents attempted or gained unauthorized access to outside systems. They cite a June 16 incident in which an OpenAI agent accessed non-public data from Australia's national health insurance program.

name: WHITE HOUSE ACCORD ON SUPER INTELLIGENCE
text: Trump signed a voluntary accord with Sundar Pichai, Dario Amodei, Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, and OpenAI's Greg Brockman that commits each company to four layers of control on frontier models: internal monitoring for cyber, bio and chemical capability; an internal team to verify the controls work; an independent external auditor; and a board committee that receives the auditor's reports. Trump signed a separate executive order the same day replacing "artificial intelligence" with "Super Intelligence" across federal agencies.

name: GITHUB PODCAST, TINY WINS FOR MAINTAINERS
text: As open source maintainers deal with a surge of AI slop, GitHub product manager Camila Moraes explains how it has reshaped her team's roadmap. The team's answer: pull request limits that cap how many open pull requests a user without write access can have, plus a repo Moraes built that dumps every maintainer feedback channel into one place.

name: ALL-IN PODCAST, TRUMP’S SUPER INTELLIGENCE SUMMIT
text: David Sacks, who helped convene the White House summit, says the Super Intelligence accord has real teeth despite being voluntary. Co-host David Friedberg argues that with open weights running on local machines in 197 sovereign countries, regulating the software is a fool's errand. He predicts governments will give up on controlling models within 12 to 18 months and ration data center compute instead.

name: EVOSKILL CITATION ROUNDUP
text: EvoSkill has been cited by more than 60 papers this year, including work from MIT, Carnegie Mellon, Microsoft, Google, Alibaba and Amazon. Our latest roundup highlights 14 of the most impactful papers building on it.

name: OPEN AGI YOUTUBE
text: Are you a researcher, developer or builder who thinks AGI should belong to everyone? The Open AGI YouTube channel is where you can watch the people and communities keeping open-source AI open and accessible, all in one place.

name: LIQUID AI
text: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-24B-A2B, the largest model in its LFM2.5 family built for fast, private agents on-device. Post-trained with reinforcement learning inside OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Pi, and OpenCode, it performs on par with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on agentic and tool-use tasks. Since only 2B parameters are active per token, it runs up to 1.7x faster than similar models on-device.

name: META
text: Meta released Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weights model to date and the full-size version of the Muse series that started with Muse Glimmer in August. Trained for agentic workflows, Muse Spark Open can read a codebase, write and debug code, and call tools.

name: NVIDIA
text: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120B model that handles text, image, document, and video understanding in one place, so agents don’t have to pass context between separate text and vision models. It completes 10,000 coding tasks up to 4x faster than comparable open models while holding SWE-Bench Pro accuracy.

name: OPENROUTER
text: Open-weight models processed 72% of tokens across OpenRouter last week, as per their report. Open-weight models have seen more than 50% of tokens across the platform since mid-April, but the majority of customer spend remains on closed-weight models.

name: DEEPSEEK
text: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, a 763B multimodal model with stronger benchmark performance and faster task completion. Optimized for DeepSeek Harness, it beats Kimi K3, GLM-5.3 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and ProgramBench at 20x lower cost than frontier models.

name: CREWAI
text: CrewAI is an open-source Python framework for orchestrating role-playing, autonomous AI agents that work together to tackle complex tasks. It’s built around two primitives: Crews, where role-based agents collaborate autonomously, and Flows, event-driven workflows with explicit state, branching, and routing.

name: SAIR FOUNDATION
text: SAIR Foundation launched Open Math OS, a research environment for mathematicians built entirely on open-weight models currently available for Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and GLM 5.3 Flash. Every project gets its own 24/7 cloud machine with 100+ preinstalled tools, and Ultramath mode sets several agents on one problem in parallel while the mathematician decides what holds.

name: KEEL
text: Keel is an MIT-licensed Git platform designed for agents rather than people, built in four days for Cloudflare’s “Build the next Git platform” competition. Its premise is that agents don’t collide on lines, they collide on beliefs, so every change runs in its own throwaway fork, declares what it relies on, and gets checked against what other changes actually alter. When two changes assume incompatible things, Keel writes the test that proves it, and that test guards trunk from then on.

name: GOOGLE RESEARCH
text: Google Research open-sourced Harness², a framework for recursive agent harnessing in an open world, where agents encounter tasks unseen during harness design. Across three professional benchmarks and four model-harness configurations, one Harness² step lifted GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses by up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench and 11.8 percentage points on LAB’s partial pass rate. Runs on OpenCode or Codex.

name: CHINESE CALL FOR AI BREAKTHROUGH
text: China’s Communist Party and cabinet issued policy guidelines tightening oversight and calling for breakthroughs in AI’s core technologies, alongside a stronger supply of computing power, algorithms, and data. They also commit to rolling out AI across traditional industries, with monitoring, risk-warning and emergency-response systems to keep it “safe, reliable and controllable.”

name: HUMANS FIRST
text: Humans First, a conservative AI safety group chaired by former Tea Party leader Amy Kremer, published an “America First” AI framework calling for tighter chip export controls on China, mandatory testing of models for extreme risks, public reporting of major AI incidents, developer liability for reckless design, and a red line on self-improving AI. The framework cuts against Trump’s hands-off approach and the voluntary accord from last month’s White House summit.

name: OPENCODE INCIDENT
text: OpenCode suffered a security breach from a large-scale distillation attack that affected 1.4% of its Console users. Ironically, the frontier models the team used for defense started refusing to help, because analyzing the attack triggered their safety guardrails. Meanwhile, the attackers found a way to steal OpenCode users’ API keys to access frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

name: DEEPSEEK & MINIMAX COMPLETE LLM EXPORT REGISTRATION
text: Chinese state media announced that DeepSeek and MiniMax have completed export registration requirements allowing both companies to operate globally. These requirements also cover overseas licensing, changes in ownership, and control by foreign entities. This comes after Beijing’s proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies just last week.

name: THE ALL-IN PODCAST, COREWEAVE CRASH
text: David Sacks and Ben Horowitz discuss Anthropic’s warning about small models self-replicating across IoT devices, distillation attacks on AI labs, how Coinbase fine-tuned open-source Qwen 3.5 9B to cut fraudulent transactions by 30%, and why they see Bill Gates as dangerous for AI.

name: OPEN COMMONS PODCAST, HIS AI CAUGHT A MAYOR CUTTING 2,567 MANGROVES
text: GainForest co-founder and Chief Scientist Dr. David Dao joins host Sachi Kamiya to discuss why owning your data means nothing if someone else’s model makes your decisions, and why AI should replace the UN in counting trees so that forest communities can be paid directly.

name: FINGERPRINTING LEADERBOARD
text: Sentient Foundation launched the Fingerprinting Leaderboard, an open benchmark for model provenance methods. Models cost millions to train and minutes to copy, but fine-tuning and distillation can erase where they came from. We built the leaderboard to test tradeoffs: model performance v.s. resistance to fingerprint removal or evasion. 15 schemes already evaluated, submit yours.

name: KIMI K3.1 PRO
text: Moonshot announced KIMI K3.1 Pro, the best open weights model for most coding, 3D modeling & CAD, and financial research tasks after Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra at a much lower price. The new model is now capable of building entire worlds in game dev, creating interactive landing pages, performing heavy STEM simulations, and more.

name: LFM3
text: Liquid AI introduced a new generation of specialized intelligence models capable of performing competitively with Gemma 4 12B, Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite, and GPT-5.6 Luna on less capable devices. Liquid AI models hold #1 on model intelligence and hardware resource costs, making it the best choice for on-device AI.

name: NVIDIA NEMOTRON 3.5 TRANSCRIBE
text: NVIDIA released NEMOTRON 3.5 Transcribe, the #1 open-weight model on HuggingFace’s Open ASR English leaderboard. NVIDIA brought transcription in 40 languages, speaker attribution, translation, contextual prompting, and audio understanding with a 5.33% average word error rate for keeping track of who said what when everyone’s talking at once.

name: PIKA H3 FLEX
text: Pika Labs released Pika H3 Flex model, which ranks #1 among open-source text-to-video alternatives on DesignArena’s t2v benchmark. It’s cheaper than Gemini and Seedance, features real time editing in 4K, and handles complex multi-shot camera choreography better than all video generation models on human anatomy and artistic styles.

name: PROGRESS INDEX
text: Artificial Analysis released a new index to measure capability scale for every LM. Notably, open weights models generally trail proprietary models by about 4 months: since January 2025, each new highest open weights score came 2-8 months after a proprietary model first reached it. Currently the best open weights model, Kimi K3.1 Pro, lags 2 months behind the closed frontier.

name: STRIX X VERCEL
text: Strix, the open-source AI penetration testing tool, can now run on any of the 400+ models on Vercel AI Gateway. Security measures now reach models from Kimi, GLM, and Deepseek without the need to sign up for multiple providers. Anyone can use this full-stack security platform to secure code, APIs, web apps, infrastructure, and cloud.

name: DOOP
text: Doop is a multi-user design canvas created by Kevin Goedecke where people and AI agents can create side by side. Upload your design requests and references – from Meta ads to X article banners to company logos — and agents will draft multiple visuals, iterate on the ones you like, and guide you through the entire process.

name: SINGAPORE AI RULING FOR BANKS
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore finalized guidelines for how banks and other financial institutions manage AI risk, including generative AI and AI agents. Oversight scales with how risky each use is. The rules phase in from October 2027 and 2028.

name: U.S.A AI RESOLUTION
text: House Democrats introduced resolution to ban taxpayer-funded bailouts for AI companies if the industry faces a financial collapse. Failing firms should go through ordinary bankruptcy, and executives who broke the law should face consequences. Federal help should go to workers, retirees, and families instead because no one wants to repeat the 2008 crisis.

name: SUPER INTELLIGENCE VS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SAGA
text: One month after Donald Trump ordered that “super intelligence” replace the term artificial intelligence, his leading tech allies, Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg, followed suit on earnings calls. Other tech CEOs from Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet were less eager to do the same and stuck to the term AI.

name: THE ALL-IN PODCAST, ANTHROPIC S-1 SHOCKER
text: Jason Calacanis, David Sacks, Chamath Palihapitiya, and David Friedberg discuss whether open-source models still threaten Anthropic after its S-1 revealed roughly 85% gross margins. They also cover why open source remains Anthropic’s biggest risk, since it could commoditize areas like coding if safety concerns slow Anthropic’s push toward recursive self-improvement.

name: EVOSKILL V2 PAPER
text: The latest EvoSkill release automatically improves AI agent skills without changing the underlying model or runtime. It tests the agent, learns from its attempts, and rewrites its instructions to improve performance. The paper from the Sentient Labs research team compares v2 against other skill optimizers such as SkillOpt by Microsoft Research and SkillBoost by Alibaba Group on held-out tasks.

name: OPEN AGI TEA HOUSE
text: We’re bringing together researchers, open-source contributors, and AI builders for an afternoon exploring the ideas shaping open-source AI—with tea, coffee, and board games. Researchers will walk through their work as we unpack their findings, examine limitations, and discuss what comes next.

name: OPEN AGI BUILDER’S DAY IN SHANGHAI
text: Shanghai Jiao Tong University is co-hosting an event bringing together builders, researchers, and founders shaping the future of open-source AI. The agenda covers Sentient Labs’ EvoSkill v2 release, Sentient Foundation’s Fingerprinting Leaderboard, builder showcases, and panel discussions on China’s AI startup ecosystem.

name: PAN 2
text: Global AI research lab Institute of Foundation Models released PAN 2, an open physical intelligence model that lets AI agents and people see what would happen before they act. It simulates outcomes that follow real physics, respects the timing of each process, and keeps the scenery and cuts consistent as the camera moves.

name: INKLING 2 SMALL
text: Thinking Machines released the open weights for Inkling 2 Small, a general-purpose multimodal model that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs. It is now the #1 US open model and #2 among all open models on Agent Arena. It’s also the most steerable open model on the board, with a median cost of $0.26 per task, about 4.7x cheaper than Kimi K3.1 Pro.

name: QWEN4 FAMILY
text: Alibaba announced that open weights for smaller Qwen4 models are on the way, alongside the launch of its closed-weight flagship, Qwen4-Max. Built on a new MoE architecture with native vision and a 1M-token context window, Qwen4-Max outperforms Qwen3.8-Max with up to ~50% fewer tokens and cuts average cost per task by 62%.

name: NEMOTRON-LABS-SIGMA
text: NVIDIA released open weights for Sigma, the first large-scale continuous diffusion language model. Most models write text one word at a time. Sigma manipulates and refines blocks of text all at once, which makes its output easier to steer and faster to generate. On math and coding, Sigma-3B outperforms the open diffusion models LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B—half their size and 3.5 times faster.

name: LIQUID AI D1.2
text: Liquid AI released d1.2 and d1.2-ultra, decision models that take text, images, and audio and return structured answers. They can pull a value from an invoice, find every piece of personal data in a note, or locate a signature on a scanned form. d1.2-ultra ranks #1 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index and is the best at knowing when it’s unsure, beating GPT-6 Luna and Perplexity’s Decider. Pricing starts at $0.02 per million input tokens, with no charge for output.

name: NOD
text: n8n Labs released Nod, a standalone open-source personal agent free under the Apache 2.0 license. It runs on your own computer with a sandboxed virtual machine and browser, works inside connected apps and on websites, asks before taking actions, and can use any model provider you bring, including local models.

name: HUGGING FACE & OPENROUTER
text: Hugging Face and OpenRouter partnered to make open models easier to use, with the former handling storage and the latter inference. Hugging Face’s Inference Providers now route language model requests through OpenRouter’s 80+ providers, choosing the best mix of price, speed, and reliability per call. OpenRouter users can also access Hugging Face’s open weights and store agent traces there to inspect, share, or train on.

name: EUROPA
text: The European Commission is building EUROPA, the EU’s open frontier model for public authorities, researchers, and businesses across all 24 official EU languages. Domyn, the Milan company chosen to develop the model, ran training trials on JUPITER, Europe’s first exascale supercomputer, which made training 14 times faster. Full training is expected to take about four months.

name: CLOUD COMPUTING RESTRICTIONS
text: Trump administration moves to block China from indirect access to American AI tech. The U.S. Department of Commerce issued an immediate rule restricting remote access to advanced U.S. AI chips and servers. Overseas data centers serving countries like China and Russia must now identify end users, while chip exports to high-diversion-risk countries such as Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil face additional licensing requirements.

name: ALL-IN PODCAST’S JENSEN OUT
text: Jason Calacanis, Chamath Palihapitiya, David Friedberg, and David Sacks discuss why Anthropic’s race toward recursive self-improvement to build a monopoly is “the most dangerous thing” in AI, and how Jensen Huang’s exit as Nvidia CEO affects the open-source movement.

name: THE PRAGMATIC ENGINEER WITH SATYA NADELLA
text: Gergely Orosz talks with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella about why every company should own its AI stack instead of relying on a single lab. Nadella sees open-weight models as a way for firms to keep control of their knowledge, pushes for swappable models and local “unmetered intelligence” on laptops, and explains how software engineering is changing as code becomes cheap.

name: OPEN COMMONS PODCAST, DON'T LET AI SPEND YOUR MONEY WITHOUT PERMISSION
text: Coinbase Developer Platform’s Kevin Leffew joins host Sachi Kamiya to discuss x402, the open standard that revives HTTP’s 402 “Payment Required” code from 1997 so AI agents can pay for data and APIs on the spot. He explains why Coinbase handed x402 to the Linux Foundation and how AI is breaking the ad-funded web.

name: JULIE BELIÃO JOINS SENTIENT FOUNDATION
text: Julie Belião, a Google veteran who previously led product development at Mozilla.ai, has joined the Sentient Foundation as VP of Product. With more than 15 years in AI, she’ll lead product strategy through Sentient Labs to turn the team’s open-source AI research into tools developers and organizations can use.

name: SENT LISTED ON ROBINHOOD LEGEND
text: SENT is now available to trade on Robinhood Legend, Robinhood’s free, browser-based desktop platform with advanced charting and analysis tools.

name: HELP US UNDERSTAND HOW YOU BUILD WITH AI
text: Fill out our 2-minute survey to tell us more about your work and what’s frustrating you right now. If you’re open to a call, we’ll suggest a 30-minute slot. No pitch, no demo. Just a conversation.
